messages:
Nora (docs): Heads-up, I submitted a consolidation PR for Dedicated capacity docs. Need: concise autoscale examples, terraform + SDK snippets, a short migration checklist, and clearer wording on SLA vs burst semantics. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4951
Ibrahim (infra): Nice. Please split examples into three flavors: reserved non-spot, spot/preemptible, and hybrid (reserved + burst). Different eviction behavior across them.
Kay (eng-runtime): From perf runs: target_cpu=58 was a good middle ground; 60 minimizes tail latency but slows scale-up. I'll add two examples and a short explanation.
Nora (docs): Sounds good. I'll annotate recommendations: "production: 60" and "cost-optimized: 55". Also added a placeholder for a quick rollback example if routing needs to be changed mid-migration.
Evan (legal): Quick reminder: public docs should say "SLA-backed for qualifying Dedicated contracts" and avoid absolutes. Keep contract-level specifics in customer agreements.
Tess (solutions): For migration checklist, customers need a preflight: IAM roles, VPC peering, and model routing policy copy. I'll draft a bullet checklist and include Terraform module example.
Nora (docs): Draft Terraform snippet in PR:
```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "main" {
  region = "us-east1"
  accelerator = "a10g"
  size = 4
  autoscale = {
    min = 2
    max = 10
    target_cpu = 60
    burst_enabled = true
  }
  eviction_policy = "none"
}
```
Can infra confirm attribute names and `eviction_policy` vs `eviction_strategy`?
Ibrahim (infra): Our provider uses `eviction_strategy`. Docs can show `eviction_policy` as a human alias but include a note mapping to provider names. For spot pools set `eviction_strategy = "preemptible"`.
link-bot: link-check: broken -> /dedicated/old-runbook (docs/dedicated/ops.md:line 24).
Nora (docs): removing that obsolete link now.
Kay (eng-runtime): Add a sample command to detect evictions: `grep -i evict /var/log/redwood/runtime.log` and a Console metric: `rate(evictions_total[5m]) > 0`. Also add a Grafana panel query: `sum(evictions_total) by (pool)`.
Tess (solutions): SDK quickstart examples (Node + Python) — can someone confirm these map to the real SDK calls? Node:
```js
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.reservations.create({ region: 'us-east1', accelerator: 'a10g', count: 4 });
```
Python:
```py
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=os.environ['RW_KEY'])
c.reservations.create(region='us-east1', accelerator='a10g', count=4)
```
Ibrahim (infra): Good for docs. Note: in internal SDK we also support `client.pools.create` alias. Add a small mapping table.
Evan (legal): Proposed SLA sentence: "Dedicated reservations are SLA-backed for qualifying contracts; performance may be affected during maintenance or large-scale infrastructure incidents." Avoid 'guarantee'.
Nora (docs): I'll include Evan's wording verbatim. Also adding an oncall quick-playbook for migrations:
- Verify reservation shows healthy in console
- Check eviction rate `evictions_total`
- If evictions > 0.2%: identify cloud spot events then switch pool to reserved or enable fallback routing
- If latency > threshold: roll back routing to previous model variant
Ibrahim (infra): Add example `journalctl -u redwood-runtime | grep -i "terminated"` for provider-initiated terminations. Also add a note that burst_enabled does NOT increase SLA-backed reserved capacity.
link-bot: spellcheck: found 'autoscaleing' -> suggest 'autoscaling' (docs/dedicated/autoscale.md:line 12).
Nora (docs): fixing typos and will merge once link-bot is green and Evan signs off on SLA text. After merge I'll open a follow-up to add a short internal-only runbook with pager escalation matrix. :rocket:
